documents.behavior: Potential data exfiltration using an unencrypted non-C2 network protocol such as HTTP.
investigation_steps: Review HTTP POST and related flow evidence.
Check file transfer metadata and receiving endpoint.
Distinguish source-file creation from transfer.
Do not treat informational HTTP alerts as proof.
Verify non-C2 channel before asserting this technique.
documents.title: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol

documents.behavior: Repeated or systematic password guesses against an authentication service such as SSH.
investigation_steps: Review authentication failures and timeline.
Correlate source, destination, account and SSH process.
Check separately for successful authentication.
Do not infer account compromise from failures alone.
documents.title: Password Guessing

documents.behavior: Potential transfer of data using HTTP POST and related network/file evidence.
insufficient_evidence_conditions: HTTP POST alone does not prove malicious exfiltration.
File creation alone does not prove that the file was transferred.
An informational HTTP server alert is not exfiltration-specific evidence.
Byte count alone does not prove the content or sensitivity of transferred data.
investigation_steps: Verify HTTP POST records using original Event IDs.
Match HTTP events and fileinfo using the original network flow ID.
Review source, destination, transfer direction and available byte counts.
Distinguish file creation from evidence of transmission.
Determine whether receiver confirmation or file integrity evidence exists.
Verify whether the transfer used a non-C2 channel before confirming T1048.003.
Separate informational alerts from evidence of data exfiltration.
recommendations: Review network destinations and expected business traffic.
Preserve flow, HTTP and file metadata for analyst verification.
Consider containment only after policy-based human approval.
documents.title: HTTP Data Exfiltration Investigation

documents.behavior: Repeated SSH authentication failures consistent with password guessing.
insufficient_evidence_conditions: Failures without success evidence do not establish account compromise.
A disconnect event alone does not establish a successful login.
investigation_steps: Verify incident source events and their original Event IDs.
Review the SSH authentication timeline and its time window.
Correlate source IP, destination IP, account and SSH process.
Check whether repeated failures originate from one or more sessions.
Search separately for successful authentication evidence.
Classify observations, unsupported claims and missing evidence.
recommendations: Review affected account and SSH access policies.
Consider rate limiting, MFA or access restrictions after analyst review.
Escalate if independent evidence of unauthorized access is found.
documents.title: SSH Brute Force Investigation

additional_evidence_to_request: Successful SSH authentication records, if available.
Session establishment and account activity records.
Independent account owner or administrator confirmation.
documents.behavior: Verification of whether SSH password guessing resulted in unauthorized access.
insufficient_evidence_conditions: Absence of success records in this dataset does not prove no compromise occurred.
investigation_steps: Confirm the reported authentication failures using source Event IDs.
Search for accepted authentication on the same target and account.
Inspect session creation and subsequent activity if logs exist.
Determine whether the available evidence proves unauthorized access.
Return insufficient evidence when success or compromise is unverified.
Request SOC Analyst review before declaring account compromise.
recommendations: Request missing authentication and session logs if needed.
Review account security and access permissions.
Do not declare compromise solely from brute-force indicators.
documents.title: SSH Account Compromise Verification

documents.behavior: Evidence-grounded triage of correlated SOC incidents.
insufficient_evidence_conditions: A MITRE document is contextual knowledge, not incident evidence.
An unsupported hypothesis must not become a confirmed finding.
Severity must not be asserted without an explained rationale.
investigation_steps: Identify incident scenario and verify incident metadata.
Review primary and supporting events in chronological order.
Check the source Event IDs behind each factual observation.
Retrieve relevant MITRE references and investigation playbooks.
Distinguish confirmed observations from hypotheses.
Assess severity using available evidence and stated assumptions.
Record missing evidence and uncertain findings explicitly.
Submit findings and recommendations for SOC Analyst review.
recommendations: Preserve original source references and investigation timeline.
Prioritize analyst verification of high-impact findings.
Document limitations and outstanding questions in the report.
documents.title: General Incident Triage
